0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 5 June 1980, after the draft finalized by the Automobile Electrical Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This standard does not recommend any enveIope dimensions of pushbutton switches but to facilitate interchangeability only the panel cut out dimension is specified. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the basic mechanical and electrical requirements and methods of tests for push-button type switches for use in automotive vehicles. These switches are normally used for starters, heaters, etc. 1.2 This specification 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. manudoes not cover the requirements for horn switches.

2.3 Type Tests - Tests carried out to prove conformity with the specification, These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a given type of push-button switch. 2.4 Acceptance Tests - Tests carried out on samples for the purpose of acceptance of the lot. taken from a lot

2.4.1 Lot - All push-button type switches of the same type, design and rating, manufactured by the same factory during the same period, using the same process and materials, offered for inspection at a time shall constitute a lot, 2.5 Routine Tests - Tests to check requirements which 3. AND CONSTRUCTION used in the construction of the switch shall

5.1 Materials - All materials be suitable for tropical use.

5.2 Constructiorm - The switches shall be so designed and constructed as to be mechanically robust and free from any operational difficulties. They shall function safely and reliably under the conditions of vibrations, shocks, etc, met with during normal installation and use. They shall have adequate resistance to corrosion, heat and humidity. 6. MARKING 6.1 Each push button the following: Name Ratings, Terminal switch shall be distinctly and indelibly marked with

7.4 Performance and Continuity Test - The force required for pressing the push-button knob to establish contact shall be between 7 and 20 N. With the switch knob depressed, the continuity between terminals shall be checked. Continuity shall break when the switch knob is released. switch shall be subjected to a flash 7.5 Flash Test - The push-button test with an ac voltage of 250 V rms at a convenient frequency between 40 and 60 Hz for a period of 5 seconds between the insulated terminal and the body. 7.5.1 Requirement - The contact without arcing or puncture. shall satisfactorily withstand this test

7.6 mV Drop Test - The switch shall be connected in a suitable circuit The voltage at the terminals adjusted to pass 10A through the contacts. shall be maintained at 7, 14 and 28 V for switches rated at 6, 12 and 24 V respectively. Three consecutive voltage drop readings ( due to contact resistance ) between the terminals shall be noted after depressing the push-button with a force of 20 N. 7.6.1 Requirement the following values: The average value of mV drop tests tests shall not exceed 80 mV 300 mV

SAMPLING A-f. LOT OF PUSH-BUTTON

A

TYPE SWITCHES

A-l.1 In any consignment all the push-button switches of the same type and manufactured in the same batch, shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-l.2 From each lot, samples shall be taken and tested for acceptance test. If a push-button switch fails in any one of the acceptance tests, it shall be called a defective. *Environmental tests for electronic equipment : Part XII Dust test. tEnvironmenta1 tests for electronic equipment : Part XVIII Salt mist test. A-2.1.1 The push-button switches shall be selected at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, the procedures given in IS : 49051968*, shall be followed. A-3. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY A-3.1 The push-button switches selected as per co1 1 and 2 of Table 1, shall be tested for all acceptance tests ( see 7.1.2.1 ). If a push-button switch fails in any one of the acceptance tests, it shall be called a defective. A lot shall be considered as conforming to the specification if the number of push-button switches failing to satisfy any one of the acceptance tests, shall not exceed the corresponding permissible number of defectives ( see co1 3 of Table 1 ).
